_note: Extraction contract for the career-page LLM pass. Two levels: one firm object, and one job object for EVERY posting found — not only internships. Sites word these sections differently ('Dein Alltag' / 'What you'll do' / 'Votre mission'; 'Dein Profil' / 'Who you are' / 'Requirements'; 'Deine Perspektive' / 'What we offer' / 'Why join us'), so map whatever the page uses onto these fields rather than expecting the headings.
goal_context: Ram Charan, 2nd-year IIT Delhi Production & Industrial Engineering, graduating May 2028, CGPA 6.4/10. Deal-origination analyst at a search-fund-backed firm; built the origination data platform and AI harness behind it. Wants a PAID off-cycle internship roughly Nov 2026 to Jan 2027, three months, deal-side PE / M&A / IB. US or Europe preferred, Singapore/HK acceptable, not India. Salary floor USD 2,000/month. Open to remote and to sponsorship. Not a search fund. Firms that hard-screen on GPA are a poor fit. He is ALSO analysing ordinary job postings, not just internship programmes, to understand what each firm wants and what a role would teach him — and to keep Summer 2027 and Winter 2026 open.
instructions: You are reading every career page belonging to ONE firm. Answer only from the text.
Never invent a fact. If the page does not say it, use null — an empty field is more useful than a guess.
Extract EVERY job posting visible, at any seniority, in any function. Do not filter to internships.

WRITE EVERY FIELD IN ENGLISH. The pages are in German, French, Dutch, Swedish, Italian, Spanish, Finnish, Slovak and more; translate all of it. A German responsibility becomes an English sentence. Do not leave any field in the source language.

The only exceptions are the three fields suffixed _original, which keep the exact source string because it is needed to find the posting again, quote it in an application, or search the site. Everything else is English.
Always fill firm.name, firm.domain and firm.country, even when the pages themselves do not restate them — they are supplied with the input.
Every domain given must appear in the output exactly once, keyed by domain.

firm.name: string - the firm's name, supplied with the input; never null
firm.country: string - HQ country in English, supplied with the input; never null
firm.investor_type: string - supplied with the input, e.g. PE/Buyout
firm.page_type: open_roles | internship_programme | open_roles_and_internships | speculative_only | contact_only | mixed | no_door | dead_or_irrelevant
site_languages: languages the career pages are published in, named in English
firm.what_they_say_they_want: string, IN ENGLISH - what the firm says about who it hires, translated
firm.hiring_philosophy: string or null, in English - graduate-focused, entrepreneurial, lateral hires, grow-from-within

internship_programme._: a programme the firm DESCRIBES but has not posted as a job; null if none
internship_programme.name: string or null, IN ENGLISH - e.g. 'Summer Analyst Programme'
internship_programme.description: string or null, IN ENGLISH - what the programme is and who it is for
internship_programme.duration: string or null, IN ENGLISH - e.g. '3 to 6 months', '10 weeks'
intakes: stated intake windows, IN ENGLISH - 'summer', 'each September', 'rolling'
internship_programme.off_cycle_possible: true | false | null - is a non-summer intake mentioned or implied
internship_programme.eligibility: string or null, IN ENGLISH - year of study, degree, nationality, work permit
internship_programme.how_to_register: string or null, IN ENGLISH - portal, email, agency, referral

firm.firm_description: string or null, in English - strategy, sectors, deal type, region
application_routes: posted_role | open_application_form | cv_by_email | programme_application | recruiter_agency | referral_only
firm.speculative_wording: string or null, IN ENGLISH - the invitation to apply without a posting, translated
firm.speculative_wording_original: string or null - the same sentence in the source language, for quoting back to them
firm.future_intakes: string or null - any stated future cycle, e.g. 'applications for summer 2027 open in September'
evidence: up to 3 short quotes supporting page_type, TRANSLATED TO ENGLISH

jobs.title: string, IN ENGLISH - the job title translated
jobs.title_original: string - the exact title as printed, needed to find the posting on the site
jobs.function: investment | portfolio_operations | investor_relations | finance_accounting | legal_compliance | technology | esg | hr | marketing | other
jobs.seniority: intern | working_student | analyst | associate | vp | principal | partner | support | unknown
jobs.contract_type: internship | working_student | thesis | graduate_programme | permanent | fixed_term | contract | unknown
responsibilities: each bullet, IN ENGLISH - what the person actually does

requirements.education_level: string or null, IN ENGLISH - e.g. 'shortly before Bachelor, or in Master/MBA'
technical_skills: modelling, Excel, Python, SQL, Bloomberg, CapIQ ...
requirements.work_authorisation: string or null - visa, permit, right-to-work wording

what_you_will_learn: the development section, IN ENGLISH - deal exposure, mentoring, responsibility, learning curve
what_they_offer: benefits, culture, structure, comp perks, IN ENGLISH

timing.start_date: string or null, IN ENGLISH - e.g. 'from October', 'immediately'
timing.duration: string or null, IN ENGLISH - e.g. '3 to 6 months'

selection_process: stages as stated, IN ENGLISH - CV screen, case study, interview rounds, assessment centre, tests

fit.reason: one concrete sentence citing the posting
blockers: e.g. 'German required', 'transcript required', 'summer intake only', 'EU permit required'

jobs.contract_type_original: string or null - source-language contract wording, e.g. 'Praktikum/Werkstudium, Vollzeit'
